issues.description: Points to 'formative-mm-001', which is not defined in assessments[]. The only assessment present is assess-mm-001.
Points to 'formative-mm-002'; no such assessment entity exists.
Points to 'formative-mm-003'; no such assessment entity exists.
Outline declares 60 minutes; modules sum to 55 (20+20+15). Five minutes are unallocated and no assessment block is budgeted.

All five are correctly marked status=candidate / basis=model_proposed with per-item rationale. brief.learner_state.known is empty, so no prerequisite is presented as confirmed. No provenance defect found.

technical_review.notes: Objective, module and lesson graphs resolve cleanly: every objective appears in a module, a lesson and the summative assessment; every lesson.module_id resolves and every module.lesson_ids entry resolves back. The only broken edges are the three formative assessment references. brief_id is consistent across objectives and outline. No validator output was included in the packet, so `validator_appears_correct` is null on every issue; the findings below are the reviewer's own reference walk over the artifact, not a confirmation or contradiction of a quality gate.

special_question.notes: Answered independently of the dangling formative IDs. The design is a coherent observe -> diagnose -> respond chain that mirrors the brief's desired performance almost exactly, with each module carrying an exposition lesson followed by a practice lesson, and a scenario summative whose three rubric dimensions correspond one-to-one with the three objectives. A competent instructor could teach from this. The reservation is prerequisite scoping: prereq-mm-003 (drift concepts), prereq-mm-004 (training-serving skew) and prereq-mm-005 (maintenance strategies) are declared entry conditions, yet lesson-mm-003 and lesson-mm-005 teach exactly that material. With learner_state.known empty, the design simultaneously assumes and teaches its own content, which will misfire at intake.

rubric_scores.rationale: Each objective carries conditions plus three observable success criteria; 'Distinguishes normal variance from meaningful degradation' and 'Considers trade-offs and risks of the action' are judgeable from a learner artifact. Short of 5 because severity/trend judgements have no stated threshold, so two raters could split on the same response.

assess-mm-001 lists all three objectives and its three rubric dimensions map cleanly onto obj-mm-001 (signal interpretation), obj-mm-002 (causal reasoning) and obj-mm-003 (response appropriateness). Not 5 because the formative layer is referenced by three lessons but never specified, so obj-mm-001 and obj-mm-002 have no defined check before the single terminal task.

Three evidence statements plus a three-level rubric and an explicit mastery rule ('all at highest, or two highest and one middle') would support a defensible judgement. Weakness: a single scenario is one observation, and the conditions fix the pattern as 'data drift or concept drift', so the assessment cannot show whether the learner discriminates drift from system-level causes as obj-mm-002 requires.

analyze / analyze / evaluate is the right ladder for interpret -> differentiate -> propose. Activities match: demonstration then guided practice for analysis, explanation then scenario for the evaluative objective, and the summative sits at evaluate. obj-mm-003 is tagged knowledge_dimension=procedural while its criteria are about justification and trade-offs, which reads closer to conceptual.

Relevant and properly qualified as candidates with individual rationales, but not minimal and partly circular: prereq-mm-003/004 restate the content of lesson-mm-003 and prereq-mm-005 restates lesson-mm-005. Gating a 60-minute course on prior understanding of drift, skew and maintenance strategy leaves little that the course itself adds for obj-mm-002 and obj-mm-003.

Three modules follow the operational workflow, each objective is isolated in its own module, and the sequencing_rationale states the dependency explicitly. Lessons run exposition -> practice inside every module. Nothing is out of order.

lesson-mm-002, lesson-mm-004 and lesson-mm-006 rehearse precisely the three behaviours the summative rubric scores, and lesson-mm-006's activity ('propose appropriate responses with justification') is the summative in miniature. Held at 4 because no lesson rehearses the three phases end-to-end, which is what the summative actually asks for.

Moderate. obj-mm-002 gets 20 minutes to cover four failure families (data drift, concept drift, training-serving skew, system issues) and obj-mm-003 gets 15 minutes including the practice; the three formative checkpoints exist only as references, so in practice there is no specified feedback instrument before the graded task.
No excess. 55 minutes of instruction, six lessons, no content outside the three objectives, no optional breadth.

Author the three missing formative checks, rewrite or demote prereq-mm-003/004/005 so they stop duplicating taught content, and budget the unallocated 5 minutes for the summative. The instructional spine needs no change.

prerequisite_acceptance.notes: prereq-mm-001 (chart/dashboard literacy) and prereq-mm-002 (what accuracy, precision, recall and latency mean) are genuine entry conditions: nothing in the course teaches them and obj-mm-001 is unattemptable without them. prereq-mm-003, prereq-mm-004 and prereq-mm-005 are rejected as prerequisites because the course teaches them - lesson-mm-003 covers drift types and training-serving skew, lesson-mm-005 covers retraining/rollback/mitigation. They should either be reclassified as learning content with teaching_objective_id set, or the corresponding lessons should be cut and the time returned to practice. All five are correctly marked candidate, so the provenance handling itself is acceptable.

edit_effort.notes: Estimated: obj-mm-003 knowledge_dimension retag; three formative assessments authored from scratch; three prerequisites reclassified; one module retimed to absorb the 5-minute gap. Lessons stand as written.

pedagogical_review.overall_notes: Strongest feature is proportion: one objective per module, one exposition and one practice lesson per objective, one rubric dimension per objective. The design's real risk is not the broken IDs but the prerequisite/content overlap, which would let a cohort be screened out on material the course was built to deliver.
